issues.summary: Number.isFinite guard lets null / '' / whitespace (and empty gweiFactor) through as 0, producing a 0n gas price instead of falling back to the next oracle or the provider fee data
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: useDefaultGasPrice.ts:55-58 and 89-95 only check Number.isFinite; Number(null) and Number('') evaluate to 0 (checked with node), so fetchGasOracle returns {gasPrice: 0n} normally. getGasPrice (line 132) then returns it without trying the next oracle, and getGasParameters never falls back to feeData. The PR sets out to reject invalid oracle values, and a JSON null is a realistic oracle response.

issues.summary: The rounding tests use inputs whose product is already an integer, so they would pass even without Math.round
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: Checked with node: 22.846685108*1e9, 20.123456789*1e9 and 25.5*1e9 are all Number.isInteger === true (test lines 247, 267). Without Math.round, BigInt() would still succeed on these inputs, so the float fix this PR claims to add has no test that would catch a regression.

issues.summary: Rounding tests compute the expected value with the same BigInt(Math.round(x*1e9)) formula as the implementation
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: test lines 256-258 and 276 derive expected values from the implementation's own expression instead of literal bigints. That makes the assertion tautological, but it has less impact than the non-fractional inputs issue above.

issues.summary: The Etherscan path can yield a negative maxPriorityFeePerGas when suggestBaseFee > FastGasPrice
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: useDefaultGasPrice.ts:69 returns maxFeePerGas - baseFee with no floor. This subtraction predates the PR (the PR only changed the conversion), and Etherscan's FastGasPrice normally includes the base fee, so this is unlikely in practice.

issues.summary: No tests for empty-string, whitespace or null oracle values
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The NaN test block (test lines 192-300) covers only undefined, non-numeric strings and a missing key. Those are the inputs the guard currently lets through, so the gap is real, but it follows from the guard issue above.

issues.summary: The test mocks global.fetch instead of using MSW
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: test lines 28-50 swap global.fetch for a jest.fn. AGENTS.md prefers MSW, but grep shows no MSW usage anywhere in packages/utils/src, so this is a minor convention mismatch that has no existing setup to follow.

issues.summary: The test hand-builds Chain with an `as unknown as Chain` cast instead of using chainBuilder()
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: test lines 22-23 use a double cast, while packages/utils/src/tests/builders/chains.ts already exports chainBuilder(). The cast skips type safety and goes against the project's faker/builder convention.

issues.summary: The multiply / isFinite / Math.round / BigInt sequence is repeated three times
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: useDefaultGasPrice.ts:55-65 and 89-95 repeat the same small pattern. Extracting a helper would be a bit cleaner, but the repetition causes no concrete defect.

issues.summary: Suggestion to export the parsing helpers and unit-test them directly
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: parseEtherscanOracleResult (line 54) is exercised through renderHook, which works. Testing it directly would be a testing-style preference, not a defect.
